scenes.title: The budget
scenes.description: The flyer is up and the stalls are filling, but after printing and supplies there is hardly anything left in the open day budget.
lines: The flyer’s up.
The stalls are filling.
Then Maya looks at the budget.
Once they’ve paid for printing and supplies, there’s hardly anything left.

scenes.title: A grant made for them
scenes.description: Maya asks the chat tool about small grants for community open days. It gives a grant name, an amount and a link, and she starts adding it to her report for Rosa.
lines: She opens the chat tool.
“Are there any small grants for community open days?”
It comes back with a grant name, an amount and a link.
The grant sounds like it was made for events exactly like theirs.
“Rosa will want to see this.”
Maya starts adding it to her report.

scenes.title: What would you check?
scenes.description: The learner is asked what they would check before Maya sends her report.
lines: Before she sends it, what would you check?
Make your choice, then carry on.

scenes.title: Page not found
scenes.description: The link leads to a missing page and a search finds nothing. The local volunteer office has never heard of the grant but offers two real schemes, so Maya takes the grant out of her report.
lines: Maya clicks the link.
Page not found.
“Maybe they moved it,” she thinks.
She searches for the grant by name.
Still nothing.
So she calls the local volunteer office and reads out the name.
“Where did you hear about that one?” the person on the phone asks.
“We don’t know of a grant by that name.
But I can send you two schemes that are open right now.”
Maya takes the grant out of her report.
The name, the amount and the web address had all sounded convincing.
She couldn’t find a funder or an official application page to back them up.

scenes.title: Real-looking, not real
scenes.description: AI answers can contain names, figures, quotes and links that look real, or information that is out of date. A leading question invites agreement; asking for the rules and where to check them gives you something to verify.
lines: An AI answer can contain names, figures, quotes and links that look real.
It can also give you information that was true once but is out of date.
And the way you ask can steer the answer.
“We qualify for this grant, right?” invites agreement.
“What are the eligibility rules, and where can I check them?” gives you something to verify.

scenes.title: Open day
scenes.description: Maya checks the funders' own pages and applies for a real grant. On open day, visitors arrive, a child plays chess, the gardening club hands out seedlings and Rosa gives Maya a thumbs-up.
lines: Maya opens the funders’ own pages, checks the criteria and deadlines, and applies for one of the grants.
On open-day morning, the first visitors come through the door.
A child sits down for a game of chess.
Someone from the gardening club hands out a seedling.
Across the hall, Rosa catches Maya’s eye and gives her a thumbs-up.

scenes.title: Money, health and the law
scenes.description: For questions about money, health or legal rights, use AI to get familiar with the topic and work out what to ask, then check with a reliable source or a qualified person before acting. The learner thinks of a question and where they would check it.
lines: When an answer could affect your money, your health or your legal rights, you can use AI to get familiar with the topic and work out what to ask.
Check the answer with a reliable source or a qualified person before you act on it.
Your turn.
Think of a question about money, health or the law you might ask an AI chat tool.
Where would you go, or who would you ask, to check the answer?
